# CPDataKit v0.9.2

CPDataKit v0.9.2 improves consistency and reliability across validation, conversion, loading,
catalog updates, and output publication.

## Highlights

- Missing string values are diagnosed during validation, so validation and HDF5 conversion agree.
  Error messages identify the field and explain how to complete the input.
- HDF5 1.0 keeps effective units and records whether they were declared, assumed from the schema,
  or inherited from historical metadata. Inspection, reports, and comparisons display that origin.
  Missing source-unit declarations produce warnings while error-free data remains valid.
- NetCDF, Zarr, and Parquet loaders accept optional `ReadLimits`. Explicit limits check source
  size and record counts; bounded Zarr loads also check directory links.
- SQLite catalog reads use a consistent error type, connections use a busy timeout and WAL,
  and concurrent partial job updates are merged inside one transaction.
- Reports, inspection output, and schema JSON are published atomically. Existing output permissions
  and platform newlines are preserved, including Windows DACLs during replacement.
- Job failures during cancellation retain an error summary and a local exception log.
- DAMASK detection preserves HDF5 opening failures, and six existing tests gain stronger assertions.
- Documentation and interface copy describe supported workflows directly.

## Validation

Local Windows / Python 3.12 validation of the fixes completed with **1409 passed, 1 skipped** and
**90.0592%** coverage. The existing skipped case requires symbolic-link creation permissions.
Ruff, distribution builds, package metadata checks, and independent Standards/Spec reviews passed.
Detailed before/after evidence is under `docs/verification/2026-09-27-review-fixes/`.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade "cpdatakit==0.9.2"
```

Python 3.12 or newer is required. Existing schema and HDF5 1.0/2.0 formats remain supported.
Start with the [Chinese workbench guide](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/main/docs/workbench-guide.md)
or the [command-line quickstart](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md).
